summary: APPROVED. I independently reran the full integration lane (4/4 pass, exit 0, 75s — AC-2 spawns the three documented commands as real pnpm subprocesses, deletes dist first, and the post-links dist tree digest matches the implementer's recorded digest exactly), pnpm typecheck (exit 0), and biome ci over the repo plus biome check on the three touched files (exit 0, clean). No mocks, skips, canned output, or test-only seams anywhere in the test file — mutations run over real copies in owned mkdtemp scratch and the original CONTRIBUTING.md re-reads byte-identical after each. Every factual claim in CONTRIBUTING.md matches the product: the seven-stage build chain equals the actual build script in apps/docs/package.json, the snippet receipt really ends with "errors": [], the link summary/soft-external-fail behavior matches scripts/docs-data/check-dist-links.ts, and the currency rule names the registry path, the description field, and reviewer judgment while explicitly denying that CI proves prose accuracy. Quadrant-pure how-to: scope and non-scope up front, PR defined on first use, imperative steps with concrete expected results, canonical links instead of duplicated standards, terminology-lock terms (registry item, description) used consistently. RED evidence is the correct missing-doc content-failure form (3 fail with named diagnostics, not module-load errors) and AC-2 passing in RED is by-design and sound: its commands are pinned to apps/docs/package.json, not to the doc. Two non-blocking notes for a future polish pass, neither rising to a fix: (1) CONTRIBUTING.md:24 'a summary line ending in 0 error(s)' — the real line ends with the warning count ('...0 error(s), 7 warning(s)'); 'reporting 0 error(s)' would be exact, though the adjacent fail-soft clause already prevents misreading. (2) The four independent criteria are formatted as a numbered list where bullets would technically fit non-sequential items; as a submission checklist the numbering is a defensible convention. Committed .tmp/ORI-CONT-006 evidence follows the established repo convention (FAM-001/002 precedent) and the writeProhibited set is untouched — only the three deliverables plus owned evidence changed.
